Rotate a point about a centre The same process, now with any angle Subtract C Rotate about zero Add C How do u and v determine U and V after a turn by theta? Inspect this rotation of the same offset Q. At 90 degrees: Q'=(-v,u), so the example gives P'=(1,3).

Rotate a point about a centre Return: put the result into the same middle operation Subtract C Rotate about zero Add C Counterclockwise theta; u=x-a, v=y-b. Same centre C=(a,b). 90-degree check: (u,v) -> (-v,u); P=(4,2), C=(2,1) -> P'=(1,3).
Rotate a point about a centre Use it: the same P and C, now 30 degrees

Rotate a point about a centre Subtract the centre. Turn the offset. Add it back. Subtract C Rotate about zero Add C Equal axis scales. Positive theta: counterclockwise; negative: clockwise. Checks: C stays fixed; distance to C stays fixed; zero turn gives P.
